title: A Google Ads click is counted as organic search, so ad signups have no channel of their own
detail: FOUND 2026-11-10 while wiring the Owner's first Google Ads campaign (Find your people locally, goal: subscriptions). first-touch already captures the gclid, but deriveChannel never read it. Google Ads auto-tagging sends a gclid, a google.com referrer and no utm, so every ad click was stamped source_search, the same as organic search. A hand-tagged utm_medium=cpc&utm_source=google was worse: the cpc rule sent it to social. CLOSED 2026-11-10: new acquisition channel paid_search (label Paid search, registry tag source_paid_search). A gclid wins after the entry routes; cpc/ppc/paid/sem from a search-engine source is paid search; cpc from a social source stays social. The channel rollup reads ACQUISITION_CHANNELS, so the new row shows with no further wiring. Conversions themselves need no code: GA4 is live in production and the Stripe webhook already sends a server-side purchase joined to the browser session (LIVE-348); the Owner links Ads to GA4 and imports the purchase key event.

verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const fail=(m)=>{console.error(m);process.exit(1)};const strip=(s)=>s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g," ").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm," ");const c=strip(fs.readFileSync("lib/attribution/channels.ts","utf8"));const r=strip(fs.readFileSync("lib/traits/registry.ts","utf8"));if(!/paid_search/.test(c))fail("no paid_search channel: a Google Ads click lands in organic search");if(!/touch\.gclid/.test(c))fail("deriveChannel ignores the gclid, so an auto-tagged ad click reads as organic search");if(!/source_paid_search/.test(r))fail("no source_paid_search registry tag, so the cohort cannot be segmented");process.exit(0)'
verify.note: Passes when a paid_search channel exists, deriveChannel reads the gclid, and the registry carries source_paid_search. Comments stripped first.
